name: correctness

findings.message: The cycle dispatch-unit skip guard reads `.stage_statuses["$_safe_cyc_id"] == "complete"` but cycles are never written to `stage_statuses` — the entire block including the DSRHYD-2 fail-closed artifact check (lines 3590-3629) is unreachable dead code, so completed cycles are always re-entered on resume and cycle-member artifact absence after rehydration is never caught.
findings.quote:
if $resume_mode && [[ -z "$skip_until_stage" ]]; then
                        local _du_cyc_status
                        # Sanitize cycle id to prevent jq injection via template-sourced values.
                        local _safe_cyc_id="${_cyc_id//[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/}"
                        _du_cyc_status="$(get_state_field "$state_file" \
                            ".stage_statuses[\"$_safe_cyc_id\"]" '' 2>/dev/null || true)"
                        if [[ "$_du_cyc_status" == "complete" ]]; then

findings.message: `_ZBUILD_FROM_STAGE_EMIT_START=true` sets `_is_resume=true`, which activates the DSCMBR-1 skip-on-complete guard for iter 1; when `--from-stage <cycle>` targets a cycle whose members already have `stage_statuses = "complete"` from prior iterations, all members are silently skipped in iter 1, no `stage.start` is emitted for any cycle member, and the cycle re-converges with zero actual dispatches — violating DSFSTG-1.

The DSCMBR-1 skip guard reads the flat `stage_statuses[$s]` map, which never resets between iterations; when the run is interrupted in the window after `_cycle_state_write_iter_start` writes `current_iter=N` but before any member of iter N has dispatched, all members show `"complete"` from iter N-1 — the skip guard fires for every member of iter N, leaving the entire iteration with zero dispatches and no `stage.start` events.
